title: Dictation
description: Local Whisper speech-to-text on the GPU: one shortcut to record, text is typed and copied
author: Frame Tweaks; engine: whisper.cpp (ggml-org), model: OpenAI Whisper
why: Typing with controller lasers is slow. The Frame's Adreno GPU transcribes locally in a few seconds, so nothing leaves the headset.

title: whisper-frame
description: groffta's dictation: hold Select or a mic under any floating window (shares dictation's model)
author: groffta (whisper-frame); SteamVR-restart fix by Frame Tweaks
why: Dictate without menus: hold the headset's Select button, straight into the window you're looking at. Its window mic is off: it costs ~31% of a CPU core and causes jitter.

title: Arrow Pad
description: Floating arrows/Home/End/F-keys/Ctrl pad with a dictation button; never steals focus
author: Frame Tweaks; look and haptics after TaiKeid's Full Keyboard
why: Steam's keyboard has no up/down arrows, Esc, Ctrl or F-keys. In VR it's a native overlay that never steals focus.

title: Full Keyboard (VR)
description: TaiKeid's full-size VR keyboard for the dashboard and desktop (checksum-verified)
author: TaiKeid (steam-frame-full-keyboard)
why: The most polished full keyboard for the Frame's VR dashboard and desktop.

title: Screen reader
description: KDE's screen reader (Orca) on in desktop mode; Meta+Alt+S toggles it
author: Frame Tweaks; Orca by GNOME
why: Orca ships with SteamOS but is off; this turns on KDE's own screen-reader setting (and puts it back on removal).

title: Shared clipboard
description: One clipboard for desktop mode and VR floating windows (clipboard-sync, built from upstream)
author: dnut (clipboard-sync); approach from lhns/steam-frame-nix
why: The Frame's VR session and its nested desktop have separate clipboards, so copy/paste between them doesn't work otherwise.

title: Android Mirror
description: Mirror and control an Android phone: aarch64 adb + scrcpy, finds the phone automatically
author: Genymobile (scrcpy), Android platform tools, Frame Tweaks launcher
why: Use your Android phone without taking the headset off. Google ships adb only for x86; this installs an aarch64 build.

title: Mouse cursor fix
description: Makes the mouse pointer visible in desktop mode
author: curiousjtuber (steam-frame-utils), originally ThrillSeeker via Cas and Chary XR
why: In desktop mode KWin draws the pointer on a hardware plane the headset doesn't show, so the mouse moves invisibly.

title: VR dashboard patching (helper)
description: Lets the VR windows tweaks adjust SteamVR's dashboard; installed automatically when needed
author: Frame Tweaks
why: SteamVR's dashboard is a web page with no settings for these behaviours; this opens its local DevTools port while SteamVR runs and injects the small patch of each VR windows tweak you install.

title: Curved world windows
description: Windows you float into the world start curved, like the dashboard (Toggle Curvature still works)
author: Frame Tweaks (approach from lhns/steam-frame-nix)
why: SteamVR has no setting for it: world windows always start flat. A tiny dashboard patch presses Toggle Curvature for you on each newly floated window.

title: Back to the previous window
description: After you float a window out of the dashboard, the dashboard shows the window it showed before (after 2.5 s) instead of an empty space
author: Frame Tweaks
why: Floating the window the dashboard shows leaves an empty space where it was. This switches back to the window you had before, the way a click on its dashboard button does.

title: Pick up when floating
description: Float in World also picks the window up for placing, like grabbing its bar; your next click (or letting go of the trigger) puts it down
author: Frame Tweaks
why: Floating a window and then grabbing its bar to place it takes two clicks; this makes it one.

title: Shared KDE wallet
description: One wallet for desktop mode and VR, desktop unlock dialog, 4-hour auto-lock, keyring for CLI tools
author: Frame Tweaks; launcher approach from lhns/steam-frame-nix
why: The Frame's two sessions each start their own KDE wallet, which overwrite each other; the stock wallet has no password; terminal tools find no keyring.

title: Signal: key in the wallet
description: Signal's database key in the wallet instead of plain text (an existing plain-text key is moved over)
author: Frame Tweaks
why: A headset gets passed around, often without a login password. Flathub Signal otherwise keeps its database key in plain text.

title: Firefox privacy
description: Strong anti-fingerprinting (resistFingerprinting, letterboxing, WebRTC limits)
author: Mozilla / Tor Project (resistFingerprinting); settings by Frame Tweaks
why: The Frame's hardware (Adreno GPU, VR-desktop window size, touch input) is rare among browsers, which makes it easy to fingerprint.

title: NordVPN (WireGuard)
description: NordVPN as NetworkManager connections with a tray icon; survives SteamOS updates
author: Frame Tweaks; uses NordVPN's servers and API
why: The usual NordVPN install goes into /usr, which every SteamOS update wipes, and the desktop has no network applet.

title: Homebrew
description: Package manager several tweaks install their programs with (into /home/linuxbrew)
author: Homebrew project
why: SteamOS's system partition is read-only and wiped by updates; Homebrew installs programs outside it, without root after setup.

title: Memory caps
description: Memory limits for heavy apps (Whisper, Android Mirror, VSCodium) so one can't freeze the headset
author: Frame Tweaks
why: A runaway app can use up the Frame's memory and stall VR; systemd can cap it per app without root.

title: Tools
description: restart-plasmashell: bring back a crashed taskbar/system tray
author: Frame Tweaks
why: In the nested desktop nothing restarts a crashed taskbar, and it has to be relaunched inside that session.

title: Menu icons
description: Icons for Konsole, System Settings and other apps that show blank in Steam's VR + menu
author: Frame Tweaks (finding from lhns/steam-frame-nix)
why: Steam only looks icons up in the hicolor theme; these apps' icons exist only in KDE's Breeze theme.

title: ydotool (helper)
description: Keystroke injection for any app; installed automatically when needed
author: ReimuNotMoe (ydotool)
why: The only way for ordinary programs to type into any app under the Frame's Wayland desktop. Installed automatically when needed.

title: VSCodium
description: VS Code without telemetry (Flathub, aarch64)
author: VSCodium project
why: Coding on the headset; Flathub has the aarch64 build.

title: Claude Code (command line)
description: Anthropic's coding agent in the terminal (claude), installed into your home folder
author: Anthropic
why: Anthropic's native installer works on SteamOS's arm64 without root and keeps itself updated.

title: Claude Desktop
description: Official Linux arm64 beta, installed and updated without apt
author: Anthropic
why: Anthropic's Linux build is a .deb; SteamOS has no apt and a read-only root, so this unpacks it into your home folder.
